newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech PM says CPI dip comes at growth's expense.
newsitem.headline: Czech PM says CPI dip comes at growth's expense.

text.p: Czech Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus said on Tuesday that the slowing in March inflation came at the cost of economic growth, and he was not pleased by it.

"It is a textbook truth that a decline in inflation is bought off by a decrease in the pace of economic growth, and I have the feeling that the price is too expensive here, and I would surely not recommend this treatment," he told Czech radio in an interview.
"I must say that unfortunately I am not joyous about it."
The Czech Statistical Bureau said earlier that inflation slowed to 0.1 percent month-on-month in March and 6.8 percent year-on-year, from 0.3 percent and 7.3 percent respectively in February.

Last month, Klaus criticised the Czech National Bank for going too far in tightening monetary policy by raising its key discount rate a full percentage point to 10.5 percent last June, while significantly increasing minimum reserve requirements on banks.

The central bank said last week that the factors which caused the monetary tightening -- mainly domestic demand caused by a sharp increase in wages -- were still present and their policy has remained unchanged.
